Explain that bradykinin accumulation is the mechanism of ACE-inhibitor cough; switch to an ARB if cough is troublesome.

Aliskiren is included mainly for conceptual completeness on Figure 8 — keep this brief and emphasize that ACE inhibitors and ARBs are the clinically dominant classes, while flagging the combination-therapy caution as a safety point worth remembering.

This slide is the clinical payoff of Figure 8 and the pregnancy/creatinine points from the ACE inhibitor slide — make the connection explicit: the drug class students might expect to avoid in kidney disease is actually the preferred therapy, precisely because of how it works at the glomerulus.
